previous_evidence: M03 B overall MAE 6.190525; prior low 650 hours MAE 5.465992 versus A 5.116743; low->low 625 hours B 4.110280 versus prior baseline about 2.79; low->above26 20 hours B underprediction 48.77161; these rise hours do not overlap actual daily maxima.
question: Can persistence only in the observable prior low state reduce overall error without worsening daily-maximum accuracy or rise underprediction?
evaluation: Reuse only existing April/May/June development predictions on identical 2184 common hours and 91 full dates. No July/August evaluation or fitting.

rule.name: B_prior_low_persistence
rule.information_time: Immediately after t-1 observation, assuming no reporting delay as in M01
rule.low_state: lag1_maximum > 0 and 20 <= floor(lag1_mean + 0.5) <= 26; same recorded-state definition as M02/M03, not a maximum-value threshold

secondary_reports: RMSE and under/over amounts and frequencies
selection.if_rejected: Retain B. Inspect origin-available inputs of prior-low rise versus stay cases; do not use target-defined transitions to select predictions and do not search thresholds for a desired conclusion. Further model changes require a concrete new development question.

interpretation: Development-stage exploratory rule and error diagnosis; no causal, alarm, maximum-time-identification, operational saving or independent-test claim. Existing low-state boundaries are inherited, not newly optimized.
